name: F-687 passphrase channels
description: How the value of --passphrase / --passphrase-stdin becomes the BIP-39 passphrase. Normative for every implementation that accepts a passphrase on a command line (mnemonic-toolkit, ms, and any port). Identical copies live in mnemonic-toolkit (crates/mnemonic-toolkit/tests/vectors/) and mnemonic-secret (crates/ms-cli/vectors/). Each case runs against the seed below; expect.fingerprint is the BIP-32 master fingerprint of BIP-39 seed(seed_phrase, passphrase).
rule: --passphrase-stdin: stdin, with exactly ONE trailing \n or \r\n removed; every other byte kept.

--passphrase @env:VAR: the value of VAR with exactly ONE trailing \n or \r\n removed (the stdin rule). VAR must match [A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*; an unset VAR is an error naming VAR; a set-but-empty VAR is the empty passphrase. Whole-value only: x@env:VAR is a literal.
--passphrase <anything else>: that literal string, verbatim, plus exactly one stderr line (argv_note); the value is never echoed.
one stdin per invocation: --passphrase - or --passphrase-stdin beside another input read from stdin is refused before anything is read.
note_env_newline: Changed by F-687 (operator, 2026-09-25: no existing wallets to preserve): before, mnemonic-toolkit took @env:VAR verbatim, so VAR=TREZOR\n derived 48efb44f while TREZOR\n on stdin derived b4e3f5ed. All three private forms now share one byte rule.
argv_note: warning: secret material on argv (--passphrase) — read it privately with --passphrase - or --passphrase-stdin (stdin), or --passphrase @env:VAR (environment variable)
seed_phrase: abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon about
